observation.visible_scene: An aerial/oblique view of a grass fire. A bright orange-yellow curved fire line burns along a band of dry tan grass on the left, enclosing a darker, partly charred interior zone. Grayish-white smoke drifts over the right half of the frame, and a separate small flame patch sits at the bottom-right corner. The scene is continuous fire activity with no people or equipment visible.
visible_changes: The tongues of the curved fire line flicker, elongate, split and merge frame to frame (deformation of the flames), while the overall position of the burning line relative to the frame edges stays roughly constant.
The smoke plume on the right shifts, thickens and thins, and its edges curl and move, indicating drifting smoke over time.
The bottom-right flame patch persists, with its own shape flickering and slightly growing/shrinking between frames.
The dark interior area between the fire line and the smoke remains largely unchanged in extent, with occasional small glowing embers visible within it.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the fire line is actively advancing, retreating, or holding position is not determinable from this short excerpt; the segment shows ongoing burning but no clear onset or completion.
The cause of ignition, wind conditions, fuel beyond the frame, and any later spread are unseen.
Whether the apparent stability of the fire line reflects true steadiness or a slow advance too small to measure here is unknown.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain: the framing of the fire line and grass band is nearly identical across frames, suggesting a mostly static or very slowly drifting camera, but the lack of fixed background references prevents confirmation.
It is unclear whether the bottom-right flames are part of the same fire front or a separate burning patch; they appear as a distinct localized flame cluster throughout.
